subject: Re: Time-to-first-token and streaming constraints — discovery notes
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Lowe <anna@clearpay.io>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-05T16:15:00Z
Subject: Post-call recap — TTFT & streaming constraints (ClearPay)

Hi Anna — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of what you told us
- Primary UX: in-browser checkout messaging (web) with a fallback mobile SDK.
- Traffic shape (ballpark): 800–1,200 reqs/min steady, peaks to ~5,000 reqs/min during promotions.
- Typical payload: 40–120 output tokens (mean ~70).
- Target TTFT SLO: 150ms p50 for small responses, 250ms p95 as acceptable for long responses.
- Streaming: prefer minimal client changes — leaning toward SSE; WebSocket is possible for persistent sessions.
- Chunk cadence: client prefers 1–3 chunk updates for initial response (priming) and then 50–150 token chunks for long outputs.

Key non-functional asks we captured
- Sustained concurrency: 100–200 concurrent sessions during normal hours, up to 800 concurrent at peak.
- Burst handling: ability to absorb 2–3x baseline for 5–10 minutes without degradation.
- Fallback: automatic degrade to smaller model/low-latency variant if TTFT > 500ms.

Immediate next steps (proposed)
1) We (Redwood) will produce a short probe plan and load profile template you can run or share sample traces for — attachment: stream_probe_template.csv.
2) Karthik to propose an initial acceptance criteria doc for TTFT/throughput and warmstart expectations.
3) Ben to run a quick feasibility check on SSE heartbeat/pacing (150ms vs 300ms) and KV cache priming strategies.
4) Anna to share a week of anonymized traffic shape or a sample trace (if possible) and confirm procurement timeline.

Deliverables & timeline
- Probe template + suggested probe script: t+1 business day (Ben)
- Acceptance criteria draft: t+2 business days (Karthik)
- Follow-up technical deep dive call: propose Tue 2026-06-09 14:00 PT (please confirm)

Attachments: stream_probe_template.csv (probe fields), clearpay_perf_profile.json (placeholder you can fill).

Thanks — will keep this short and action-focused.

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai

From: Anna Lowe <anna@clearpay.io>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-05T17:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — TTFT & streaming constraints (ClearPay)

Thanks Vanessa — this looks great and matches our notes. A few clarifications and additions: 

Traffic specifics
- The 5k/min peak is on the US region and lasts ~10–12 minutes during promos; otherwise we sit ~900–1.1k/min.
- Concurrency: 120 typical, spikes to ~700 concurrent sessions.
- Average generated tokens per user event: 72 (SD ~30).

Latency expectations
- Our primary requirement is p50 TTFT <= 175ms for short responses (under 60 tokens). p95 <= 300ms if feasible. Anything above 500ms will cause visible UX regressions.

Streaming protocol
- SSE preferred since we can patch the browser client quicker; however we also have a subset of customers using long-lived sockets for a persistent experience (WS). We need both options supported as rollout will be phased.
- Heartbeat: we can accept 250–300ms heartbeat for SSE provided network jitter handling is robust.

Chunking / priming
- We do some prompt priming on the server side; hope Redwood can support prefix/KV caching.
- Chunk size: initial quick priming chunk preferred to be <30 tokens, then steady-state 80–150 tokens.

Acceptance criteria: we'll sign off on a small pilot if p50 TTFT <200ms and p95 <350ms under a synthetic probe that mirrors our peak concurrence.

I'll upload a redacted sample trace to Drive (link below) and loop in procurement separately. Our procurement point: procurement@clearpay.io — they may ask for SOC2 and data residency docs.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1example

Available for Tue 14:00 PT. Thanks for the quick follow up.

—Anna
Anna Lowe
Sr. Engineering Manager, ClearPay
anna@clearpay.io

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Lowe <anna@clearpay.io>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-05T18:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — TTFT & streaming constraints (ClearPay)

Appreciate the details Anna — helpful. A few technical notes and a lightweight plan we can execute before the Tue deep dive: 

Notes
- SSE vs WS: operationally SSE is easier for browser-only rollouts because no connection upgrade is needed; WS gives lower overhead for many small messages if you want very low per-chunk overhead. We'll prototype both with identical backend routing and compare TTFT delta.
- Heartbeat choice: 150ms heartbeats are tight and increase CPU for many connections. Recommend starting at 250–300ms for SSE in the pilot, with instrumentation to measure reconnection rates.
- KV prefix priming: we can support prefix/KV cache warmstarts. For best TTFT we recommend a small priming call for high-frequency users (warm session cache) — reduces first generation token cost.
- Chunk cadence: our pilots show 40–120 token steady chunks hit the sweet spot for throughput vs latency. We can support the initial <30-token priming chunk followed by 80-token steady chunks.

Probe template and acceptance criteria
- Attached: stream_probe_template.csv (probe dimensions).
- Acceptance criteria doc: high-level checks we'll run programmatically: p50 TTFT < 200ms, p95 < 350ms, error rate < 0.5% during 2x burst for 10 minutes. Will produce a doc soon (ttft_acceptance_criteria.docx).

Quick feasibility execs
- I will run a lightweight internal probe (SSE 250ms heartbeat, WS persistent) against a 2x burst profile to estimate required OOM/GPU concurrency and expected cost per 1k requests. Expect to have a numbers snapshot by EOD tomorrow.

Questions for you (Anna)
- Can you share any client-side connection limits per browser (e.g., are customers behind corp proxies)?
- Any restrictions on long-lived websockets from your CDN/provider?

Thanks — will bring probe results and cost estimates to Tue.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Anna Lowe <anna@clearpay.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-06T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — TTFT & streaming constraints (ClearPay)

Ben — thanks. A couple quick answers and the sample trace link: 

- Client limits: our browser clients are standard; some enterprise customers sit behind aggressive proxies that drop idle WS connections after ~2 minutes. SSE seems to survive better across those environments.
- CDN: we use FastEdge — they allow long-lived connections but rate-limit concurrent sockets per origin in some regions.

Sample trace uploaded (redacted): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1example
I'll also loop in procurement separately (procurement@clearpay.io). They will request a SOC2 questionnaire and a draft contract; likely timeline 2–3 weeks for legal review.

Available Tue 14:00 PT — confirmed.

—Anna

Action summary for internal owners after Anna's upload and confirmation: 

Owners & tasks
- Ben: run SSE vs WS microprobe with the provided sample trace (use 250ms heartbeat for SSE and a WS persistent baseline). Deliverable: probe report + cost estimate (EOD 2026-06-08).
- Ben: include KV-cache warmstart run for a cohort of 1,000 synthetic warm sessions and compare TTFT delta.
- Karthik: draft ttft_acceptance_criteria.docx and a short canary checklist for rollout (t+2 business days — 2026-06-08).
- Vanessa: coordinate procurement intro and confirm SOC2 pickup; add procurement@clearpay.io to the HubSpot deal.

Pilot acceptance: recommended pilot pass if p50 TTFT <= 200ms and p95 <= 350ms under a 1.5x synthetic replay of peak for 10 minutes, error-rate <0.5%. If failing, fallback plan: use smaller model variant + aggressive KV priming.

Meeting: confirm Tue 2026-06-09 14:00 PT for tech deep dive. I'll prepare a short slide with metrics to compare SSE/WS and a suggested rollout timeline.

—Karthik
